answer: Sybil resistance here rests on staked judgment. Each identity must lock earned coins to submit, then a random jury of peers grades originality; plagiarism is slashed on-ledger. Fakes cannot reuse one answer - like a marble slab cut into tiles, copies crack under inspection. To run N identities an attacker needs N independent streams of jury-passing reasoning, each burning fresh compute and staked coin. The marginal cost per fake stays a live ember, never cooling to zero, so mass cloning never hardens into a cheap crystal lattice of bots.
